name: Kelp forest
notes: Cool rocky coasts with kelp canopies offshore: shoreline carries salt-spray cushions, rockweed and coastal scrub; underwater giant kelp, bull kelp and Laminaria form the forest with understory red/brown algae. Drawn on California/Pacific NW, Tasmania/NZ, Chile and North Atlantic (Norway, Scotland); underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Bull kelp

traits.trunk: long woody or soft climbing stem on a host
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: kelp: 30-60 smooth strap blades to 4 m trailing from the float, drawn as straps

bark.note: alga; smooth rope-like stipe, no bark

canopy.silhouette: long rope stipe to a bulb float trailing long straps

growth.juvenile_note: Microscopic gametophytes overwinter on rock; in late winter a tiny sporophyte appears as one flat blade on a thread-like stipe with a small claw-like holdfast. The stipe lengthens and swells at the top into a hollow ball float, the blade splits into two tufts of ribbon blades (30-64 in all, up to 4 m), and a whip-like stipe up to 36 m lifts the float to the surface by summer.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nereocystis (usually annual, sometimes persisting up to 18 months; to 36 m; blades grow up to 15 cm/day, 30-64 blades to 4 m; single large pneumatocyst; sori form on the blades and drop to the seafloor at maturity); seasonal timing from Pacific NW kelp-bed studies

fruiting.source: Kelp has no flowers or fruit: 'flowers/fruit' are the dark sori, oblong spore patches on the blades that mature in summer-autumn and then cut themselves out and sink, releasing swimming spores near the parent (Wikipedia; Amsler & Neushul). Bull kelp blades are eaten (pickled). Sizes and timings estimated

canopy.source: underwater — Macrocystis pyrifera, California, Chile, S Africa, Tasmania/NZ rocky bottom 5-30 m, fronds to 45 m reaching the surface — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Macrocystis pyrifera, California, Chile, S Africa, Tasmania/NZ rocky bottom 5-30 m, fronds to 45 m reaching

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: kelp: corrugated toothed blades 30-90 cm alternate along the stipe, each on a gas bladder

canopy.silhouette: towering brown vine of bladdered blades to the surface

growth.juvenile_note: Spores settle and grow into microscopic gametophytes; the young sporophyte is a single thin, ruffled golden-brown strap blade on a tiny stipe and claw-like holdfast. The primary blade tears repeatedly from the base into separate blades that each grow a gas bulb and a stipe, so the plantlet becomes a bunch of fronds rising to the surface. Under a closed canopy juveniles stall until light returns.
growth.source: Wikipedia Macrocystis (grows up to 60 cm/day, fronds live ~100 days, young kelp with 1-2 primary blades that split, sporophylls at the base); Kinlan et al. 2003 J. Phycol. (arrested development of microscopic stages in low light); North 1994 (individuals live several years, up to ~7)

fruiting.source: Kelp has no flowers or fruit: 'flowers/fruit' are the fertile sporophylls, short blades without gas bladders in a bunch just above the holdfast, whose dark-brown sori release swimming spores into the water. 23-155 sporophylls per plant, fertile year-round (Fernandez et al. 2021, NZ reproductive phenology). Sorus timings and decay estimated.

canopy.name: Oarweed
canopy.source: underwater — Laminaria digitata (L. hyperborea deeper), N Atlantic rocky subtidal, fingered blade 1-3 m — Wikipedia

traits.trunk: long woody or soft climbing stem on a host

leaf.note: kelp: broad blade split into 5-12 finger-like straps on a flexible stipe

canopy.silhouette: broad hand-split brown blade on a flexible stipe

growth.juvenile_note: Microscopic spores settle within a day and grow into microscopic gametophytes; young sporophytes appear as tiny brown, undivided strap blades on a thread-like stalk, splitting into finger-like straps as the blade widens. Each winter-spring a new blade grows from the stipe-blade junction (up to 1.3 cm a day), pushing the worn old blade off its tip; the holdfast is a conical tangle of rhizoids.
growth.source: MarLIN species review (Laminaria digitata: growth 1.3 cm/day Feb-Jul, slower Aug-Jan; lives 4-6 yr; sporophytes mature at 18-20 months; zoospores settle within 24 h; recruits all year; standing crop recovers in 18-20 months, full recovery ~25 months; 2-4 m); Wikipedia (sori over central blade).

fruiting.source: Kelp has no flowers or fruit: this block treats the sori (dark, slightly raised spore patches over the central blade) as flower and fruit. MarLIN (sori all year, peaks Jul-Aug and Nov-Dec; zoospores released into the water). Sorus size and timings estimated; blades eaten cooked or dried.

traits.native_range: underwater — Durvillaea antarctica, Chile, NZ and subantarctic exposed rocky shores, thick honeycombed fronds 3-10 m — W

leaf.note: thick leathery honeycombed fronds splitting into long straps

canopy.silhouette: thick leathery brown straps thrashing from a wave-battered holdfast

growth.juvenile_note: Fertilised eggs settle on bare wave-swept rock within days and grow into tiny discs; the juvenile is a small, simple, smooth strap blade on a short stalk above a sucker-like holdfast. Only later does the blade thicken, fill with buoyant honeycomb tissue and split into many long, leathery, golden-brown whip-like straps that thrash in the surf.
growth.source: Wikipedia Durvillaea antarctica (huge, tenacious holdfast; long leathery honeycombed blades; a large plant releases 100 million eggs in 12 h, mostly in winter; eggs settle close by in calm-moderate water; detached plants raft up to 210 days and 10,000 km; eaten as cochayuyo). Growth rate, maturity and lifespan estimated from bull-kelp literature.

fruiting.source: A kelp has no flowers or fruit: values map its sunken conceptacles (1-3 mm pits over the blades) that release eggs or sperm into the sea, mostly in winter (Wikipedia: 100 million eggs in 12 h). Rot time is for torn fertile blades cast ashore; counts are conceptacles per plant. Timings estimated; blades are eaten cooked as cochayuyo.

shrub.silhouette: low dense heather mound, purple haze in flower

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seeds need light and sprout in 2-6 weeks on bare peat, sand or burnt ground. The seedling is a tiny green sprig of minute, overlapping, scale-like leaves in four rows; it branches into a small upright bush (pioneer phase), then a dense, rounded dome (building phase) that later spreads, thins and opens in the centre as it ages.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Calluna vulgaris (pioneer 0-6 yr, building 6-14, mature 14-25, degenerate after 25; lives about 30-40 yr on dry heaths; seeds rarely germinate without light; highly shade-intolerant); Gimingham 1960 Biological Flora of the British Isles.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers Jul-Sep, mauve, in racemes; capsule); FEIS (flowers Jul-Nov in N America, wind and animal dispersal, seed bank long-lived); Gimingham 1960 (bees and wind pollinate; capsules ripen in autumn and shed seed over winter); counts approximate.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny plumed achenes land on bare mineral soil and sprout in 2-4 weeks. The seedling has two small round cotyledons, then small, glossy, bright-green, wedge-shaped leaves with a few teeth, over a deep taproot. It branches quickly from the base into a dense, rounded or sprawling mound of stiff, crowded green twigs.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Baccharis pilularis (germination mostly within 15-30 d without pretreatment, shade-intolerant, poor seedling growth in shade, individuals live 10-15 yr but basal sprouting and layering extend it); first flowering age estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (dioecious, flowers Jul-Oct, 55 insect visitor species incl. honey bees, achenes 1-2 mm with 6-10 mm pappus, ripe Sep-Nov, dispersed Oct-Jan); counts are flower heads, estimated.

shrub.name: Salal
shrub.source: Gaultheria shallon, Pacific NW headlands, evergreen shrub 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: Gaultheria shallon, Pacific NW headlands, evergreen shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: dense glossy thicket, leaves held flat and layered

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedlings on rotting logs and stumps (light needed to germinate): two small cotyledons, then leathery, finely toothed oval leaves. Very slow at first (only 8-13 cm after 2-3 years); then spreads by layering and rhizomes into a thicket of zigzag, reddish, glandular-hairy stems with glossy, thick, egg-shaped evergreen leaves.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Gaultheria shallon): germination in 27-45 days, light required; seedlings slow, 3-5 in after 2-3 yr; flowers only at >=5 yr; twigs live 16+ yr and rhizomes for centuries; shade-tolerant but less vigorous under dense canopy.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (flowers May-Jul, white to pink urn-shaped flowers on terminal bracteate racemes, ~6 per twig, bee and fly pollinated; hairy blue-black pseudoberries 6-10 mm ripen Aug-Oct and may persist to December, ~126 seeds each; regular good crops). Fruit set, rot and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two narrow, fleshy green cotyledons, then short, fleshy, finger-like leaves that are grey-green and often woolly. It branches low into a small succulent sprig and within a few years becomes a woody-based, mounded to sprawling grey-green subshrub on coastal bluffs, dunes and salt-marsh edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia Suaeda taxifolia (shrub or subshrub to ~1.5 m, woody below, fleshy hairy-waxy leaves; flowers 1-3 per cluster with leaf-like bracts, no petals, fleshy calyx; fruit a utricle in the calyx; salt marsh, beach, dune and scrub of S California and Baja). Germination, growth, flowering season and ages estimated from shrubby Suaeda.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Suaeda taxifolia (petal-less flowers with fleshy hairy sepals, 1-3 per cluster; fruit a utricle enclosed by the calyx). Flowering months, wind/self pollination, ripening (one shiny dark seed ~1.5-2 mm) and crop estimated from Suaeda and other coastal chenopods.

growth.juvenile_note: Spores settle within 2 days and form a tiny pink calcified crust within 3; the first jointed fronds rise from the crust after about 3 weeks and the first full segment takes ~13 weeks. The young plant is a small pink-purple crust sprouting stiff, jointed, feather-branched chalky fronds that thicken into a turf; fronds may be shed and regrow from the perennial crust.
growth.source: MarLIN species review (Corallina officinalis: fronds grow 2.2 mm/month at 12-18 C, 0.2 at 6 C; fronds up to 12 cm; spore settlement 48 h, crust 72 h, fronds 3 weeks, first segment 13 weeks; crust perennial; new fronds within 6 months, 10% cover in 12 months on cleared rock; shade-tolerant understorey alga)

growth.juvenile_note: Spores drip down the grooved blades at low tide and settle close to the parent; microscopic gametophytes overwinter on rock, mussels or barnacles. Recruitment timing, growth and die-off estimated from kelp field studies.
